channel.title: CNA's Blog
channel.description: Building a portable XNA-style framework for the long term.

item.title: CNA Project Roadmap and the Path to 1.0

item.title: Performance Checklist for CNA Games
item.description: Measure and improve CNA frame time, rendering, assets, allocation, audio and loading without optimizing from intuition alone.

item.description: A staged checklist for translating an original XNA 4.0 game to CNA while preserving behavior and producing evidence after every milestone.

item.description: Plan a C# MonoGame or FNA migration to CNA by separating language translation, API compatibility, content conversion and renderer evidence.

item.description: Add a CNA renderer through the registry, capability profiles, resource contracts and shared parity fixtures instead of scattering backend branches.

item.description: Implement CNA's platform contracts for lifecycle, windows, events and optional host services without leaking native APIs into framework modules.

item.title: Packaging and Installing CNA Applications
item.description: Turn a working CNA build into a relocatable application with content, runtime dependencies, platform metadata and reproducible release checks.

item.description: Follow a CNA Game from construction and initialization through content loading, update, drawing, suspension and ordered teardown.

item.description: Select CNA texture formats by data meaning, renderer support and memory cost instead of assuming every backend accepts every SurfaceFormat.

item.title: Lighting, Shadows and PBR in CNA
item.description: Progress from BasicEffect lighting to shadow maps and CNA's optional physically based material workflow.

item.title: Render Targets and Post-processing in CNA
item.description: Use CNA render targets safely for offscreen scenes, scaling, multiple passes, MSAA, mipmaps and full-screen effects.

item.title: Debugging Graphics Across CNA Renderers
item.description: Reduce a cross-renderer CNA graphics difference to a shared fixture, capability decision or documented backend limitation.

item.title: Models, Animation and Skinning in CNA
item.description: Load CNA models, traverse meshes and bones, play animation clips and render weighted vertices with SkinnedEffect.

item.title: 3D Rendering in CNA
item.description: Assemble a CNA 3D frame from vertex buffers, camera matrices, depth state, effects and explicit draw calls.

item.description: Build efficient CNA 2D scenes with SpriteBatch, textures, fonts, transforms, blending and explicit render state.

item.title: Building a Multiplayer Game with CNA
item.description: Turn CNA's XNA-style networking and gamer services into a bounded, testable multiplayer game protocol.

item.title: Saving Games in CNA
item.description: Use CNA storage APIs to build versioned, atomic and portable save files without depending on desktop paths.

item.title: CNA on Android and iOS
item.description: Mobile CNA games must integrate lifecycle, touch, orientation, safe areas, storage and permissions in addition to cross-compiling C++.

item.title: Bringing a CNA Game to the Web
item.description: Move a CNA game to Emscripten with WebGL 2 or WebGPU while adapting its loop, assets, storage, audio and input to browser rules.

item.title: Headless Games and Servers with CNA
item.description: Run CNA simulation, tests and dedicated server logic without a window, GPU, sound device or SDL dependency.

item.title: The CNA Software Renderer
item.description: CNA's CPU rasterizer renders real pixels without a GPU and serves as a deterministic graphics oracle, CI backend and terminal presentation source.

item.title: Writing Portable Shaders in CNA
item.description: Build a CNA ShaderEffect package for OpenGL, SDL_GPU and WebGPU without confusing portable source shaders with compiled XNA effects.

item.title: Audio in CNA
item.description: CNA provides XNA-style sound effects, instances, music, microphones and 3D audio across SDL3, ALSA and silent test backends.

item.title: Input Extensions in CNA
item.description: CNA extends XNA input with text and IME events, relative mouse controls, modern gamepad metadata, raw joysticks, force feedback, device enumeration, sensors, power and clipboard access.

item.title: Device Extensions in CNA
item.description: CNA::Devices adds portable access to power, locale, clipboard, URLs, display information, native dialogs, tray icons, message boxes and cameras without extending the XNA namespace.

item.title: ASCII and CRT Effects
item.description: CNA's optional graphics extensions can turn a completed scene into a colored glyph grid or emulate scanlines, RGB masks, curvature and vignette on a CRT display.

item.title: Platform Terminal
item.description: CNA's POSIX Terminal platform presents the software renderer's RGBA framebuffer as an ANSI character grid, with keyboard, mouse, resize and honest capability reporting.
